what: The sticky header slides up and hides by exactly the amount scrolled down (up to its own height · option), and slides back down by the amount scrolled up — tied to scroll distance, not time, so scrolling slowly hides it slowly. Once the footer top passes above the screen, the header is pushed up further by the overshoot so it never overlaps the footer. When fully hidden it gets is-tucked, and the pushed amount is exposed as --fx-pushed (for aligning the top of the sticky side panel)

options.max: Max shift (px), default is element height — Brand is 116 at 1440 width (122 at 375 phone width)
options.foot: Footer selector, default footer · none means no footer adjustment
options.--fx-pushed: The currently pushed amount (px) that the part writes onto the element — used to make a sticky filter follow down, like top: calc(100px − min(var(--fx-pushed), 40px))
options.is-tucked: Marker added to element when fully hidden

from.where: shared.js .tn-nav (original main.js globalnav: on every lenis scroll c = min(rpx(116), max(0, c + Δ) − max(−rpx(116), min(0, footer top edge))) · translate3d(0, −c, 0), no transition · sticky filter top = rpx(60) + rpx(40) − min(c, rpx(40)))

note: On phones the original gets the same feel by swapping absolute positions (stick·fix), but the part uses one formula. Where lenis is used, lenis moves the window scroll so it sticks as is
